rows.note: This is the all-purpose choice when someone talks on and on or prattles excessively.

example.english: They babble as soon as they open their mouth, leaving me no chance to get a word in.
example.traditional: 佢一開口就講個不停，搞到我冇得插嘴。
example.jyutping: keoi5 jat1 hoi1 hau2 zau6 gong2 go3 bat1 ting4 gaau2 dou3 ngo5 mou5 dak1 caap3 zeoi2

rows.jyutping: gong2 je5 gong2 dou3 ham4 wu2 bat1 cing1
rows.note: Use this when the speaker's words are too indistinct or unintelligible to understand.

example.english: They babble so indistinctly that I can't understand a word.
example.traditional: 佢講嘢講到含糊不清，我完全聽唔明。
example.jyutping: keoi5 gong2 je5 gong2 dou3 ham4 wu2 bat1 cing1 ngo5 jyun4 cyun4 teng1 m4 ming4

rows.note: Use this mainly for the continuous murmuring sound of a stream or running water, not for ordinary human chatter.

example.english: The stream seems to babble as it runs over the stones; it sounds soothing.
example.traditional: 溪水喺石頭間潺潺流過，聽落好舒服。
example.jyutping: kai1 seoi2 hai2 sek6 tau4 gaan1 saan4 saan4 lau4 gwo3 teng1 lok6 hou2 syu1 fuk6
